evidence.text: Tomorrow is the first time management speaks to the Novartis/BMS autoimmune CAR-T pause, which happened after the 7 August guide -- Novartis began holding eight rap-cel trials on 24 August after three IEC-HS deaths, disclosed 1 September, and OXB fell 14.7% that day and a further 5.1% the next with no RNS of its own. The sell-side quantification is small and survivable: c.10-16m of annual clinical revenue at risk (7-10m Novartis, 2-6m BMS), autoimmune 13% of 48 programmes, and pre-booked manufacturing slots protecting FY2026 with disruption pushed to new bookings in H2 2027. Reiterating 180-200m six weeks after cutting to it is the base case and is not what the 1-2 September tape priced.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line that has moved this stock all year and it has moved it down: -14.6% on 7 Aug 2026 when FY26 went from 220-240m to 180-200m (591 to 505 on 6.6m shares), and -5.12% on the 26 Mar 2026 prelims. OXB has not had a positive scheduled-release reaction in the observed record, which is why this is sized as a relief rather than a re-rating.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock is 472p against 524p on 28 August, so roughly half the Novartis/BMS drawdown is still in the price six weeks on, and the company has said nothing -- its RNS record between 14 August and today contains one Total Voting Rights notice and four Holding(s) in Company, no trading statement. If the market believed FY26 was protected by pre-booked slots it would have closed the 1-2 September gap. Against it: the cell-and-gene CDMO sector is in genuine retrenchment (Rentschler withdrawing, Catalent closing Belgium, Charles River divesting its CDMO to GI Partners, Lonza reporting softer cell-and-gene), which is a broader public series and is the reason the low end of my band is -3.5 rather than -1.

evidence.text: The company's own 23 July RNS pre-announces H1 adjusted EPS of 38p-42p and, in a footnote, puts FY2026 consensus at 202.8p -- so the 'in line' the market is holding requires roughly 162p of H2 adjusted EPS, about four times H1 and an ~80/20 split, against 141.4p/133.9p (51/49) in 2025; the same RNS reports the order book at 17.3 weeks, which reads as improvement only against the FY25 year-end 15.7 but is flat against the like-for-like H1 2025 comparator of 17.4 weeks printed in the same sentence, and on a sales base 21% lower is roughly 21% smaller in absolute terms, with order intake down 11%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Judges has downgraded or disappointed at three of its last five scheduled statements and the stock moved -11.61% (Trading Update 2024-11-18), -15.19% (Half Year Trading Update 2025-07-24) and about -11% (Full Year Trading Statement 2026-01-22, Proactive) on those days -- so when this line surprises on this name it surprises double-digit and the UK tail is not truncated. But the two September interims in the observed RNS history moved only -4.27% (2024-09-19) and +1.91% (2025-09-18), because the July trading update had already carried the half-year news both times; and the 2026-07-23 update itself, which contained the 38-42p, the -21% revenue and the Geotek slip to 2028, moved the stock only -1.62% (4625.0 -> 4550.0, Yahoo daily closes) and it closed higher the next day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 202.8p footnote and the 38-42p are both public, but no source I could reach does the division. Every piece of secondary coverage I found reported the flattering order-book comparator (Sharecast/Halifax and the Stockopedia brief both frame it as '17.3 weeks compared with 15.7 weeks at the end of 2025') and none states the implied H2 EPS or the 80/20 split. This is a 4-analyst, GBP 250m AIM name trading about USD 446k a day, so the marginal price-setter is a retail or adviser reader of exactly that wire summary. If the arithmetic were priced you would not see all four published targets sitting above spot (average 6450p, Berenberg buy 5600p reiterated 25 July 2026, and even Jefferies' underperform target of 4015p is 7% above the 3750p spot) and you would not see the whole 19% de-rating since 23 July happen on a median 8,030 shares a day with no analyst revision in between.
evidence.independence: Separately corroborated as a fact pattern by the company's 22 January 2026 statement, which guided FY2026 to 200-250p explicitly 'assuming no rebound in US demand and no contribution from Geotek's next coring expedition' -- and the July RNS then pushed that expedition from early 2027 to 'no earlier than 2028', so the FY26 bar has not moved while the 2027 support under it has been removed: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/judges-scientific-says-starts-2026-with-lower-than-desired-order-book-ce7e58d2de8ff725 (2026-01-22). Note this finding deliberately merges what were two sizes in my pre-local draft (the H2 arithmetic and the order-book framing) because both rest on the same RNS document.

evidence.text: The Investegate regulated-news record shows Judges has filed nothing price-sensitive in the 61 days since it reaffirmed FY2026 -- only a Notice of Investor Presentation (12 Aug) and two Share Incentive Plan PDMR notices (6 Aug, 10 Sep) -- from an issuer that publishes its own consensus number and has a demonstrated habit of putting bad news out in a standalone RNS, which under MAR Article 17 makes two months of silence evidence the board does not presently believe 202.8p is materially unachievable.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three times this board concluded it would miss, it said so in a dedicated RNS and the stock fell double digits the same morning (2024-11-18 -11.61%, 2025-07-24 -15.19%, 2026-01-22 about -11%). The two times it reached September interims without having warned first, the reaction was -4.27% (2024) and +1.91% (2025). So the informative event for this name has historically been the warning RNS, not the results RNS.
evidence.why_not_priced: An absence is not a headline and no aggregator emits it; you can only establish it from a complete domestic RNS mirror, which is what Investegate is. The price is behaving as if a warning were coming -- the stock is at 3750p, 2.7% off its 52-week low of 3650p and 41% below the 6360p high, having fallen 19% from 4625p on 22 July -- but it got there on a median 8,030 shares a day (about GBP 300k), which is a thin tape with no bid rather than a market verdict. If the market had weighed the silence you would expect the drift to have stopped or reversed as the 30-day closed period began around 24 August; instead the stock made new lows on 16, 17, 21 and 22 September. With three estimates on the tape there is no published model of Signet's tariff line to revise. If it were priced you would see a tariff-relief note among the handful of SIG previews; instead the only visible preview thesis is Citi's generic 'inline Q2, raise to the top end', which is about demand, not landed cost. Slow-burning: Signet's ~$2.0bn inventory against ~$4bn COGS means post-July-24 landings mostly hit Q4/Q1 P&L, which is why I size it small.
evidence.independence: Jewelry-specific confirmation of the rates and effective date from National Jeweler (https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/15165-new-trump-tariffs-what-they-mean-for-jewelry), which puts India/China/Thailand/HK/UAE at 12.5% and Canada/Mexico/Pakistan/Sri Lanka/UK at 10% — note it disagrees with a 10% figure reported for India elsewhere, so I treat the step-down as 2.5–5 points rather than a point estimate. evidence.text: Paychex's FY2027 guidance, set 2026-06-25, explicitly assumes 'no further changes to the Fed funds rate' and on that basis guides interest on funds held for clients DOWN to $195-205m from FY2026's $210.9m; the Fed then HIKED 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023, with the dot plot at 4.00-4.25% for both year-end 2026 and 2027 and markets pricing a further hike.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the exact line the stock trades on. On 2026-06-24 PAYX beat on both revenue (+12%) and adjusted EPS ($1.32) and fell 1.72% purely because the FY27 guide — of which this interest line was a named drag — sat below the street's ~8%. On 2025-06-25 the FY26 guide took the stock down 9.4%. The baseline's seven reactions are 4 down / 3 up with a 1.72% median, and the down days are guide days.
evidence.why_not_priced: PAYX fell over the five sessions spanning the 16 September hike (sealed run_up_5d_pct -3.91%), so the market read a hiking Fed purely as a small-business demand negative and did not mark up a ~100%-margin float line that the company had guided down on an assumption the hike has now falsified. If this were priced, PAYX would have outperformed payroll peers after 16 September and the client-funds line would appear in the previews; the previews are entirely about hiring freezes. The dollars are deliberately sized small: per the 31 Aug 2025 10-Q the float is $4.98bn available-for-sale against only $775.2m of money-market and restricted cash equivalents, so ~86% of the portfolio reprices on the ladder rather than with Fed funds, making the direct FY27 benefit roughly $2-5m of a $195-205m line. What is worth more than the dollars is that a guided line gets revised the right way on a day the market is braced for the wrong way.
evidence.independence: The FOMC decision itself is a separate primary source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html (2026-09-16). ADP set its own FY27 interest assumptions off 'Fed Funds futures contracts and various forward yield curves as of July 28, 2026' (https://mediacenter.adp.com/2026-07-29-ADP-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2026-Results), so the whole payroll-float complex is carrying a pre-hike rate assumption, not just Paychex. NOTE: this finding shares the client-funds line with finding 3 below; they are the forward and the trailing leg of the same line and are deliberately signed opposite, not double-counted.

evidence.text: Paychex publishes its own free monthly Small Business Employment Watch, and it covers exactly the June-August quarter about to be reported: June 2026 printed a jobs index of 99.83, the highest since August 2025 and a fourth consecutive monthly improvement, and August printed 99.13, in line with the 2026 year-to-date average of 99.20, with weekly hours growth positive for a sixth straight month — so the 'flat employment levels' assumption underpinning the FY27 guide held through the reported quarter even as the stock lost 9.79% in 20 days on hiring-freeze fear.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Filed as guidance rather than reported_quarter deliberately: on 2026-06-24 this name beat both reported lines and still fell 2.3%, and the sweep row states a reported-quarter beat here is worth close to zero. What this series actually settles is reaffirm-versus-cut on the annual guide, and the guide is what moved the stock -1.72% in June 2026 and -9.4% in June 2025. The counterweight is resolved inside this finding rather than left to argue against it: the index deteriorated WITHIN the quarter, from 99.83 in June to roughly 99.23 in July to 99.13 in August, so the data supports a guide that is reaffirmed and does NOT support one that is raised. Paychex has historically reaffirmed rather than raised at Q1 in any case. That is why this is [sizing note removed].7 and not at the +1.4 a clean reading of the quarter alone would have carried.
evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown has a named cause and it is a large-cap narrative, not this company's book: PAYX fell 3.9% in a single session on 2026-09-08 on fears that corporate hiring freezes would spread to small business. If the market were weighting Paychex's own client-base index over that narrative, the stock could not have fallen 3.9% in a session in the month after its own index printed a twelve-month high for the first month of the quarter being reported. The August release is at https://www.stocktitan.net/news/PAYX/stable-employment-levels-continue-for-u-s-small-businesses-in-k2eaefz17ugv.html (2026-09-01). Sized modestly because this is a free company press release on an 18-analyst, $41bn name — the opposite of the thin-coverage setup where an unpriced fact moves a stock hard.

Cutting the other way, and stated rather than hidden: ADP's National Employment Report put small businesses under 50 employees at just +3,000 jobs in August with total private payrolls +38,000, the smallest since January (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/02/private-payrolls-rose-by-38000-in-august-fewer-than-expected-adp-reports.html).
